limitations: This create-only request is an explicit closure over the discovery assignment; an empty reviewer_added_requests array means no reviewer-added candidates were found.
Ranking evidence and candidate material fingerprints are copied exactly from the bound discovery capsule and do not replace final source review.

reviewer_added_requests.discovery_reason: Backend-change-builder selects redacted diagnostics and may change backend logging while proving implementation closure, whereas logging-design-gate owns logging-schema, redaction, diagnostic-gap, and independent logging-verdict decisions. Full material is required to determine when the bounded implementation must hand off to the logging gate rather than treating redacted observability as sufficient closure.

Backend-change-builder implements authorization, tenant, untrusted-input, disclosure, and mutation behavior, while security-privacy-gate owns reachable abuse paths, trust-boundary changes, denied-path evidence, and the security verdict. Full material is required to establish the implementation-versus-independent-gate boundary for backend changes with security impact.

Business-invariant-analysis identifies permission and tenant invariants, authoritative owners, enforcement points, and bypasses, while permission-boundary-modeling defines subject-resource-action conditions, trusted policy inputs, reachable enforcement, denial semantics, and negative proof. Full material is required to separate discovery of a business invariant from construction of the authoritative permission contract.

Controller-api-implementation maps transport input, trusted context, application results, responses, and errors according to an existing contract and explicitly excludes contract decisions, while api-contract-design owns resource semantics, requests, responses, errors, compatibility, and consumer proof. Full material is required to verify the design-to-implementation handoff when a controller change exposes an unresolved API contract choice.

Domain-event-modeling owns business fact meaning, producer and commit boundary, payload identity, ordering expectations, and consumer responsibilities, while message-queue-design owns broker topology, acknowledgement, retries, dead letters, replay, backpressure, and terminal disposition. Full material is required to distinguish event semantics from delivery mechanics where ordering, duplicates, replay, and consumers overlap.

Domain-event-modeling includes payload compatibility and consumer responsibilities, while version-compatibility owns consumer inventory, mixed-version matrices, migration mechanisms, retirement evidence, and rollback readability. The lightweight boundary cannot establish when event-local schema evolution becomes a system compatibility decision, so full candidate material is required.

Domain-logic-implementation owns rule authority, invariants, transitions, typed denials, and bypass protection and may encounter permission or entitlement rules, while permission-boundary-modeling owns authoritative subject-resource-action policy and reachable enforcement. Full material is required to determine when a domain policy remains ordinary business logic and when it must be governed as a permission boundary.

Threat-modeling owns attacker capability, reachable abuse paths, protected outcomes, control placement, and bypass analysis but excludes identity derivation, while authentication-authorization owns authenticated-subject authority, provenance, propagation, freshness, and the authorization handoff. Full material is required to verify the route from a threat-model control need to the identity-context contract without letting either skill absorb the other.

Use-case-modeling owns actor goal, system responsibility, preconditions, decision paths, guarantees, side effects, and acceptance trace while explicitly excluding detailed UI flow, whereas user-flow-modeling owns journey entry, branches, interruptions, recovery, re-entry, and user-visible authority outcomes. Full candidate material is required to verify the domain-use-case versus experience-flow handoff.

User-role-identification produces a descriptive actor and role inventory and explicitly says persona context and role evidence are not authorization or enforcement proof, while permission-boundary-modeling owns authoritative policy inputs, enforcement reachability, denial semantics, and negative proof. Despite weak lexical ranking, full material is required to protect this critical role-inventory versus permission-authority boundary.
